takeaway: Keratocanthoma: a benign volcano-like lesion on sun-exposed skin that grows over weeks and resolves spontaneously over 4 to 6 months.

question.text: An 82-year-old retired woman had a facial skin lesion for 2 months. It has now disappeared. What is the diagnosis?
question.say: An eighty-two-year-old retired woman presents with a two-month history of a facial skin lesion. The lesion has now disappeared. What is the diagnosis?

lines.text: A facial skin lesion that lasted 2 months.
lines.say: This eighty-two-year-old retired woman had a facial skin lesion for two months.

lines.text: A volcano-like bump on sun-exposed skin, typical of middle-aged and elderly people.
lines.say: It was a volcano-like bump on sun-exposed skin, typical of middle-aged and elderly people.

lines.text: A keratocanthoma grows rapidly over a few weeks to months.
lines.say: A keratocanthoma grows rapidly, over a few weeks to months.

lines.text: Then it resolves by itself over 4 to 6 months: goodbye, volcano!
lines.say: (laugh) Then it simply resolves by itself, over four to six months. Goodbye, volcano!

lines.text: It is benign and arises from the pilosebaceous glands, but it looks like squamous cell carcinoma.
lines.say: It is benign, arising from the pilosebaceous glands, though it closely resembles squamous cell carcinoma.

lines.text: Remember: a volcano-like bump that vanishes by itself is a keratocanthoma.
lines.say: Remember: a volcano-like bump that vanishes by itself is a keratocanthoma.
